subject: Pilot success signal inventory & ownership — Quantico.ai
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Turner <alicia@quantico.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot success signal inventory & ownership — Quantico.ai

Hi Alicia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a concrete next step so we stay aligned heading into the pilot kickoff. I captured the items we discussed and proposed owners/timelines below. Please review and flag anything that’s missing or off.

Pilot context (one-liner): Quantico will run a 4-week production-simulated pilot to evaluate Redwood inference for QA-assistant generation across their internal ticket backlog.

Primary success signal categories (what we'll measure):
- Latency: P95 token latency for 512-token responses; target <= 220ms on Dedicated-256 profile. Owner: Redwood (Ben). Measurement cadence: daily.
- Throughput: Sustained concurrent request rate of 200 QPS with <5% tail latency spike days. Owner: Quantico infra (Alicia) + Redwood ops for shaping. Stress test window: week 1 and week 3.
- Cost per token: Effective cost/token for production mix (docs+chats) aiming for <= $0.0009/token (including batching and prefix cache). Owner: Redwood finance contact (Laura). Reporting: weekly.
- Quality: Automated accuracy metric on a 200-case eval set (EM and top-1 F1) with human review for drift. Acceptance: >= 86% EM and no >5% regression vs. baseline. Owner: Quantico product.
- Error budget & reliability: <2% request error rate (5xx/timeout). Owner: Redwood SRE (Ben).

Deliverables & timeline:
- Day 0 (kickoff): baseline run and perf profile (responsibility: Redwood ops)
- Week 1: smoke load test; collect latency/throughput samples (both)
- Week 2: quality eval on 200-case set and initial human sampling (Quantico product)
- Week 3: cost/runbook review and optimization pass (Redwood + Quantico)
- Week 4: readout and recommendation doc (shared Drive link)

Immediate asks from you: 1) confirm owners above and 2) share sample load profile (QPS distribution) and the 200-case evaluation set by Friday so we can pre-seed tests.

Attachments: I attached a starter spreadsheet (quantico-pilot-success-signals.xlsx) that lists metrics and a column for measurement method. Also included a sample_load_profile.json stub for the traffic shape we discussed.

If that looks good I’ll schedule the kickoff (suggest Tue May 25, 10:00am PT) and loop in SRE for pre-provisioning.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Turner <alicia@quantico.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 13:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Pilot success signal inventory & ownership — Quantico.ai

Thanks Priyom — this is very helpful and matches what we talked through. A few quick notes: 

- Owners: confirmed — Quantico infra will own throughput at the infra level, product will own quality. I’ll be primary infra point for coordination.
- Load/profile: I’m attaching a trimmed set (we’ll send full in Drive) but the sample_load_profile.json you attached looks aligned to our shape (spiky morning ramp, steady mid-day).
- Cost: our CFO asks if we can include an estimate for 95th percentile daily spend as a placeholder. If Redwood can provide a run of expected costs at the target throughput/batching config that would be perfect.
- Timeline: Tue May 25 at 10am PT works for kickoff. Please confirm invite.

Two small changes to quality acceptance: can we make the baseline requirement 85% EM (instead of 86%) but require a human-reviewed drift threshold of 4%? Product is more comfortable with that band.

I’ll upload the 200-case set to the Drive link you shared by EOD Fri.

Best,
Alicia
Head of Platform, Quantico.ai

Ben/Laura — forwarding Alicia’s confirmation and a couple of actionable asks for ops and finance before kickoff next week. High-level: Quantico asked for a 95th percentile daily spend estimate and an initial P95 latency run for the Dedicated-256 profile with our default batching. Can we get the following pre-kickoff deliverables?

Action items (owner / due):
- Ben: run a simulated baseline on the Dedicated-256 config using the attached sample_load_profile.json and return a one-pager with P50/P95/P99 latency and a recommended batching window. Due: Mon May 24 EOD. (Attaching the load stub to this thread.)
- Laura: coarse cost projection for two scenarios (steady 200 QPS; bursty 300 QPS) including token estimate and expected spend (95th percentile daily). Due: Mon May 24 noon.

Notes: keep the run deterministic — use the 512 token median response length for costing. If you need a runner VM from Quantico to mirror network conditions we can request it in the kickoff.

Ben/Laura reply inline please — I’ll finalize the calendar invite for Tue after we confirm owners.

Thanks,
Priyom

On Fri, May 21, 2027 at 09:18 AM Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ben/Laura — forwarding Alicia’s confirmation and a couple of actionable asks for ops and finance before kickoff next week.

Quick update from my side — I ran a deterministic baseline against Dedicated-256 using the sample_load_profile.json and the 512-token response length you specified. Summary below (full CSV attached in Drive):

- P50 latency: 88ms
- P95 latency: 205ms
- P99 latency: 410ms (observed during two brief concurrency spikes)
- Sustained throughput: handled 220 QPS with <3% 5xx/timeouts in our isolated runs
- Recommended batching: 8–12ms preference window with prefix cache enabled — gives best tradeoff on cost vs tail latency

I’ll hand the raw logs to the finance sheet for token calculations. Laura — ping me if you want the raw trace to parameterize cost model.

Next steps I propose before kickoff: 
1) Priyom to send calendar invite for Tue May 25, 10:00am PT.
2) Laura to post the cost projection to the Drive doc.
3) Alicia to upload the 200-case eval set.

I’ll join the kickoff and bring SRE for pre-provision checks.

— Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
